title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila

title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila

title: Control of walking direction by descending and dopaminergic neurons in Drosophila
quote: SS02553 activated flies increased their walking speed immediately after the onset of activation.
mapping_basis: Name DNp17 matches the MANC type DNp17, but the kit maps the name 'DNp17' (flywire/hemibrain/malecns) to two types (DNp17, DNut046) and lists SS02553 as AMBIGUOUS DNp17;DNut046. The paper's anatomy (6 neurons per hemisphere, mainly wing and haltere neuropils) does not clearly separate them, so I chose the exact-name match; DNut046 remains possible.
stimulation: 625 nm red LEDs, 0.4-4.1 mW/cm2 (five intensities: 0.4, 1.4, 2.3, 3.2, 4.1), 9 trials each
type_coverage: full line; DNp17 population of 6 neurons per hemisphere
penetrance: significantly faster forward walking and higher tortuosity than empty>CsChrimson controls at all intensities
notes: Increased locomotion in a free-walking arena without leg tracking, so legs coded yes with confidence capped at medium. The line labels 7 non-DN types besides DNp17 (none described as DN), so specificity is minor_offtarget. The paper itself attributes the phenotype to DopaMeander rather than DNp17 (Fig. 3; see record p2-steering-0014). Sex not stated for activation experiments. Expression coded bilateral (whole split line).

title: Control of walking direction by descending and dopaminergic neurons in Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 3C-H; Results ('DNp17 is unlikely to drive fast forward walking')
quote: DopaMeander, and not DNp17, is responsible for the forward walking and turning phenotype
mapping_basis: Name DNp17 matches the MANC type DNp17, but the kit maps the name 'DNp17' to two types (DNp17, DNut046) and lists SS02553 as AMBIGUOUS. The paper's anatomy (6 neurons per hemisphere, wing/haltere neuropils) does not clearly separate them, so I chose the exact-name match.
stimulation: 625 nm red LEDs, up to 4.1 mW/cm2; data averaged across 9 trials at 4.1 mW/cm2
type_coverage: stochastic SPARC2 subsets of the SS02553 population
other_cell_types: other SS02553 types (brain interneurons 3, 4, 7; ascending neurons 5, 8; VNC local neuron 6) in some flies
penetrance: DNp17-expressing flies showed a broad range of forward velocities (1-12 mm/s, median 5 mm/s); DNp17 without DopaMeander significantly slower than DNp17 + DopaMeander
n_flies_note: 26 flies analysed: 17 with expression in some labelled neurons, 9 with none; per-group counts not read
notes: Coded as no clear DNp17-specific effect: the authors conclude DopaMeander, not DNp17, drives the forward-walking and turning phenotype. In the text I read, DNp17-only flies were not statistically compared with no-expression controls, so 'none' and 'no_visible_effect' are an interpretation. Legs unclear because flies walked at variable speeds and there was no leg tracking.
